items.title: Rock & Roll Hall of Fame ceremony full of emotions as Phil Collins, Queen Latifah, more inducted
items.summary_auto: Saturday night's Rock & Roll Hall of Came ceremony brought out stars and emotional tributes as Phil Collins, Billy Idol, Luther Vandross, Wu-Tang Clan, Queen Latifah, Oasis, MC Lyte, Sade, Joy Division/New Order and Iron Maiden were inducted during the ceremony at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, along with producer Rick Rubin.

items.title: Quebec Premier and PM Carney discuss U.S. trade, homelessness at first meeting in Cambodia
items.summary_auto: St-Pierre Plamondon said the meeting ended with federal support for the province's fight against homelessness, and the exchange of personal phone numbers. The premier also thanked the Prime Minister for his support of an economic summit that will take place in Quebec in 2027.

items.title: 'He lived and breathed it': NCAA football prospect from N.S. has died
items.summary_auto: A Nova Scotian who was set to play football at an American powerhouse college is being remembered for his exceptional talent and desire to get better on the field, but his happy-go-lucky and teddy-bear nature off of it.

items.title: Carney cites her award-winning book on encampments. She's eyeing his plan to end homelessness
items.summary_auto: One of Canada's leading authors on homelessness says the prime minister’s plan to end it within 10 years is an "ambitious goal" that has potential, but won't actually go all the way.

items.title: Senior Hamas commander who helped oversee Oct. 7 attack killed in Israeli strike in Gaza
items.summary_auto: Hamas said on Sunday that a senior commander who helped plan and oversee the Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel had been killed in an Israeli airstrike, with the Israeli military confirming his death.

items.title: We tested 6 popular apps to see what data they collect and share: CBC's Marketplace Cheat Sheet
items.summary_auto: The CBC's Marketplace rounds up the consumer and health news you need from the week.

items.title: It started with a lobster supper. Now it's an East Coast institution
items.summary_auto: The Shore Club in Hubbards, N.S., has spent more than eight decades serving up classic lobster suppers and live music to people from around the globe. A new CBC documentary pulls back the curtain on how the Harnish family managed to turn a rural dance hall into a Maritime institution.

items.title: A man was once murdered over the pronunciation of 'Newfoundland'
items.summary_auto: Newfoundlanders and Labradorians tend to feel strongly about the right way to pronounce the name of our island, but would you kill a man over it? In 1876, someone did.

items.title: Canada's health-care spending tops $10,000 per person this year. Where is the money going?
Facing 'uncomfortable' questions, King Charles shows the 'soft power' of the Crown
items.summary_auto: As with trips to Canada in 2025 and the United States earlier this year, King Charles's recent visit to the Caribbean saw him walking something of a diplomatic tightrope at a politically charged time. There seems to be an emerging pattern.

items.title: English was the language I built my career in. In Canada, it became something to prove
items.summary_auto: Anusuya Datta had never given a second thought to knowing English, having always written and spoken in the language. After moving to Saskatchewan, people continually remarked on her English skills, both in complimentary and derogatory ways.

items.title: Scientists race to discover and protect what lives in the ocean
items.summary_auto: Scientists say not knowing what lives in our oceans holds back efforts to protect them. Marine biologists are racing to catalogue species — from carnivorous sponges to otherworldly sea slugs. Here's a closer look at the creatures hidden in our seas and how humans rely on them more than most realize.

items.title: Why researchers are using drones to keep polar bears and people apart
items.summary_auto: While studies have shown drone hazing to be effective on black bears, researchers are now trying to see if it works with polar bears — a bigger, more curious and more aggressive species. The goal is to adapt the technology to Canada's North and try to take some of the risk out of managing the bears.

items.title: 3 months after mass entry, some 15,000 migrants remain in Ceuta
items.summary_auto: Three months after the mass entry into Ceuta, many migrants still hope the Spanish enclave will offer them a route to mainland Europe. Local authorities and residents are struggling with the surge.

items.title: Has treatment for stuttering been off base? New guidelines go beyond speech to the brain
items.summary_auto: More than 80 million people worldwide stutter, yet misconceptions on it persist in the medical field, and access to appropriate care can be limited. New international medical guidelines aim to change that.

items.title: Canada is spending more than ever on health care. Are we getting our money's worth?
items.summary_auto: Canada is spending more on health care than ever. Whether Canadians are getting more care for their money is another question. A new report from the Canadian Institute for Health Information (CIHI) projects health-care spending will reach a record $433 billion in 2026, or $10,398 per person, an increase of 4.8 per cent over last year.

items.title: Canada's Dabrowski, Brazil's Stefani fall in doubles semifinals at WTA Finals
items.summary_auto: Canadian Gabriela Dabrowski's unbeaten run at the WTA Finals came to an end Saturday night as she and partner Luisa Stefani of Brazil were beaten in the doubles semifinals in Indian Wells, Calif.

items.title: Nova Scotia's MacDougall uses 5-point 8th end to win mixed curling nationals
items.summary_auto: Nova Scotia's Brent MacDougall is the Canadian mixed curling champion. The Nova Scotia rink, down 5-4 entering the eighth and final end, scored five to defeat New Brunswick's Sylvie Quillian 9-5 in Saturday's gold-medal final in Woodstock, P.E.I.

items.title: Stranded B.C. flyers out thousands amid flight cancellations due to Friday's ground stop
items.summary_auto: Some frustrated Air Canada passengers say spotty communication and a lack of rebooking help has left them paying thousands out of pocket amid widespread flight cancellations due to the FAA-ordered ground stop Friday.

items.title: Fifth soldier dead from injuries suffered in CFB Wainwright fire, officials say
items.summary_auto: A fifth soldier, Pte. William Douglas Dal Bianco, has died as a result of the fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta, the Department of National Defence says.

items.title: Avian flu outbreak spreads to other provinces at national poultry show: CFIA
items.summary_auto: Avian flu has been detected in three flocks, including in Manitoba and Alberta, following an outbreak at a national poultry show in Saskatchewan earlier this month, the Canadian Food Inspection Agency has told CBC News.

items.title: New Orleans port sues for control of China-linked tanker that crashed into cruise ship
items.summary_auto: Just hours after a tanker in New Orleans lost its steering and slammed into a docked river cruise boat, the city's port sued to make sure federal investigators can seize the vessel that is owned by a subsidiary of a Chinese company.

items.title: European security plan floated by U.S. would benefit Putin, Zelenskyy says
items.summary_auto: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the United States had raised the possibility of a new security framework for Europe as part of efforts to end Russia’s war in Ukraine, warning that Moscow could use such discussions to weaken NATO and reshape the continent’s borders.

items.title: Gorgeous, heartrending Club Kid is hitting Canadian theatres. Read our TIFF review
items.summary_auto: Hitting Canadian theatres now, Club Kid is without doubt a major work. It was without doubt one of the best films at this year's Toronto International Film Festival. And while there is some doubt here, Club Kid just might make you cry.

items.title: SpaceX Starship successfully re-docks at Texas launch pad after orbiting Earth
items.summary_auto: SpaceX's Starship made a triumphant return to Earth on Saturday, caught in midair by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier. It's the first key recovery of the rocket system's centerpiece vessel in the company's decade-long effort to ‌develop a fully reusable rocket.

items.title: Carney says he will not boycott APEC 'family photo' with Putin
items.summary_auto: Prime Minister Mark Carney says he will participate in an upcoming group photo with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit out of respect for the host, Chinese President Xi Jinping.

items.title: Margaret Atwood joins other bird lovers to fight against a proposed 600-foot tower on Pelee Island
items.summary_auto: Atwood called the location, which is one road over from the new Atwood-Gibson Bird Centre, "one of the stupidest places on the planet" to put a tower.

items.title: Change to Ontario's 'safer-supply' opioid prescriptions abruptly paused due to legal challenge
items.summary_auto: A controversial change to "safer-supply" opioid prescriptions in Ontario that would force recipients to take them in front of a pharmacist, rather than on their own schedule at home, has been abruptly paused due to a legal challenge. Critics said the proposal would drastically affect the lives of drug users while causing potential chaos at pharmacies.
